art.prompt: A single wide 16:9 cinematic photorealistic frame for grounded Chinese survival horror game opening, first-person from driver of ordinary older left-hand-drive Chinese compact sedan, low driver eye view on a late summer rainy night on a narrow winding unmarked village mountain road in southern inland China. Through windshield the headlights reveal sharply textured wet rippled asphalt, gritty road shoulder, roadside weeds, old reflector post, rural forest, distant tiny incandescent village watchman's window on right. Authentic old steering wheel and worn black dashboard along bottom fifth only, very dim amber instrument cluster, simple mirror top, realistic subtle droplets and wipe streaks on glass but wiped clear at center. Focus on road, strong fine depth and materials, quietly ominous, muted blue black outside, warm dull headlights, still readable in dark. Composition centered vanishing point, drivable road, no subjects or figures anywhere, no text no captions no logos no embedded overlays, no letterbox bars, no wiper arms visible. Single continuous shot, not a storyboard.

A prop archive PHOTOGRAPH of an actual traditional Chinese funeral offering PAPER SERVANT EFFIGY 纸扎纸人, front-facing bust, isolated on transparent background. It must be instantaneously obvious this is a hollow bamboo-and-paper ARTIFACT, fundamentally NONHUMAN in construction and proportions, not an actor or a person wearing makeup or a mask. Match the supplied flat ochre PAPER face, identical stamped circle design, single vermilion circle on the left of the picture and two overlapping worn circles on the right. Folk handmade 纸扎童子 in the paper offering shops of a small Chinese village. Oversize faceted octagonal flat-carton head fixed to a very narrow exposed bamboo-stick neck, glued flaps around the sides of head, flat black INK brush eyebrows above hollow black almond eye cutouts, flat broad thin vermilion painted crescent mouth. Boxy folded black PAPER cap with scarlet paper button at the apex, absolutely NO hair or teeth or fleshy lips or eyeballs or skin. Rectangular hollow square-shouldered torso built from cream tissue pasted on a visibly angular bamboo lattice, cut-paper indigo and faded cinnabar Chinese shroud with flat glued overlapping crossed collar, cut-paper peony & longevity patterns, gold foil piping and red diamond knots. One ripped shoulder corner exposes bamboo sticks, paper twine, and the empty darkness inside; a tilted head fixed on skewed bamboo. Harsh low-angle headlight catching paper fibres and glossy glue seams, crude geometry age and water tide marks. Frame includes the whole cap and both shoulders and the full upper chest, not cropped sides. Grave, eerie quiet smile. Physical macro detail, dark moody practical lighting. NOT a living human, NOT humanoid skin, NOT wet hair, NOT a human in costume, NOT a porcelain doll, NOT a digital cartoon. No letters no logos.

Cinematic practical prop photography for a Chinese folk horror game. ONE vertical contact sheet of exactly THREE landscape panels stacked from top to bottom with equal height, edge-to-edge no gaps, no borders no letters no text. 2:3 overall portrait aspect, each shot 2:1. Depict the EXACT Chinese funeral paper effigy in the reference emerging from a wet stone well at night. Match the unmistakable folk paper craft closely, exact battered black folded cap red paper button, angular paper head and stamped flat red cheeks, black almond holes for eyes, flat red thin smile, exposed bamboo, faded ochre robe printed with indigo and cinnabar flowers, gold piping and attached red knots. This is a wretched empty paper funeral offering, inanimate materials acting impossibly. No human or performer, no hair skin or fleshy hands whatsoever. SET: round old grey carved stone well in a brick-walled rural Chinese courtyard, wooden horizontal windlass with thin hemp rope on two posts behind, glancing blue-black rain night and a warm kitchen light from right giving chiaroscuro. Shoot as if first person witness closeup with the dark hole behind the rim. TOP PANEL: macro of a folded paper mitten HAND with four folded paper strips for fingers curled over the front stone lip. One fingertip is torn and a slim bamboo splint is visible, drops glistening on coarse paper and stone, the body is still down deep and no head is visible. MIDDLE PANEL: pull back, BOTH flat paper hands now gripping the stone rim, paper coat cuffs match the reference. Behind the rim only the folded BLACK CAP RED BUTTON and brow of the EFFIGY is slowly emerging, sharp silhouette against dark negative space. BOTTOM PANEL: taller now, same exact effigy's angular paper face ABOVE the rim, looking directly at camera, red pressed cheek stamps and flat ink smile, narrow exposed bamboo neck, hollow decorated shoulders with hole showing bamboo lattice and wet paper joined with joss paper, both hands bearing down on lip. Its weight bends the paper elbow and splays the folds. Professional cinematic photography, photographic paper fiber detail, coherent geography lighting and scale. Face in center of last frame and reference proportions, not a person in a costume. Cut exactly at 1/3 and 2/3 of the height.
